objective: Port netty-codec-http2 4.2.19.Final (io.netty.handler.codec.http2) to Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2 with the original names, structure, comments and tests.

ownerDecisions: Project, folder and assembly names are the namespace root of the module (owner decision 2026-11-19, see docs/codec-base-porting.md): each codec module takes the namespace of its main package, and the tests use <project>.Tests like the other test projects.

Owner decisions 2026-11-19 for the codec modules that only need codec-base: one project per Maven module; codec-socks is Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Socks (its Maven and JPMS name) and holds the socks and socksx namespaces; haproxy is HAProxy (the casing of the Java types in that package); socksx, v4 and v5 are Socksx, V4 and V5.

Owner decisions 2026-11-25 for codec-http2: the project and namespace are Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2 (one project per Maven module; it references Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http); io.netty.util.collection stays the BCL Dictionary (the 2026-11-19 decision, revisited here as planned): Http2Settings, which extends CharObjectHashMap<Long> in Java, is built on Dictionary<char, long>, keeps its own Java methods (headerTableSize() and the others) and inherits the BCL members, and the IntObjectHashMap users keep Dictionary<int, V>; Dictionary enumerates in insertion order, so SETTINGS entries (frames and the HTTP2-Settings header) may be written in another order than Java's hash-slot order, which carries no meaning because a SETTINGS frame holds each identifier once.

statusMeaning.verified: Every declared original test is mapped to a C# test with the same name (case may differ) and passes.
statusMeaning.clr-adapted: Ported with the original names, structure and comments; every CLR difference is stated in a // CLR: comment and in this entry. For tests, some original methods are CLR-inapplicable with recorded evidence.
statusMeaning.deprecated-not-ported: @Deprecated Java unit (or a helper serving one) that is not ported; the deprecation facts, reason, replacement and every original comment/test are recorded.
statusMeaning.jvm-only-replaced: JVM-only metadata or documentation unit replaced by its recorded CLR counterpart.
statusMeaning.library-not-ported: Owner decision 2026-11-23: a unit that needs a third-party Java library with no BCL counterpart on .NET 10 (or a test of such a unit) is not ported; the library, reason and every original comment/test are recorded.

review.scope: Public abstract generic class AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder<T, B> where T : Http2ConnectionHandler where B : AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder<T, B>, the self-typed Java generic; self() casts this through object. The protected non-final Java methods are protected virtual and keep the Java overload pairs (getter InitialSettings() and setter InitialSettings(Http2Settings), ...); a Java subclass widens them to public with @Override, which a C# override cannot ("An override declaration can't change the accessibility of the virtual method"), so subclasses expose them as public members declared new that call base. The Boolean/Integer/Long fields and locals that may be null are bool?/int?/long?; SensitivityDetector is IHttp2HeadersEncoder.ISensitivityDetector and ALWAYS_VERIFY IHttp2PromisedRequestVerifier.ALWAYS_VERIFY. The @Deprecated initialHuffmanDecodeCapacity(int) ("Huffman decoding no longer depends on having a decode capacity.") names no replacement and is ported with [Obsolete] (owner decision 2026-11-16). IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException, IllegalStateException InvalidOperationException, Throwable Exception and assert Debug.Assert; a long or boolean concatenated into an exception text uses Http2CodecUtil.ToJavaString. build(decoder, encoder, initialSettings) throws Exception in Java; the C# abstract method declares nothing.

The C# DefaultChannelPipeline only runs on the Transport's AbstractChannel, which folds Channel.Unsafe into the channel (owner decision 2026-11-16, docs/transport-porting.md), so the class derives from AbstractChannel instead of implementing Channel. The folded Unsafe operations are protected internal virtual (owner decision 2026-11-25, docs/transport-porting.md "Overridable Unsafe"; overrides in another assembly "have protected access", https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/keywords/protected-internal), so the Java Http2ChannelUnsafe is a nested class with the Java code and the channel overrides AbstractChannel's WriteTransportAsync (write), FlushTransport (flush), Close (close(promise)), CloseForcibly (closeForcibly), DisconnectTransportAsync (disconnect), DeregisterTransportAsync (deregister), BeginRead (beginRead), BindTransportAsync and ConnectTransportAsync (bind/connect, NotSupportedException) with its members; each operation completes a promise of its own (Http2CodecUtil.NewPromise, without asynchronous continuations) from the parent write's own outcome, as Java does. isWritable(), bytesBeforeUnwritable() and bytesBeforeWritable() override the virtual AbstractChannel members with Java's totalPendingSize/unwritable fields (Interlocked for the atomic field updaters); the writes never reach AbstractChannel's ChannelOutboundBuffer (Java's outboundBuffer() returns null). Channel.unsafe() is the internal Unsafe(), which Http2MultiplexHandler, Http2StreamChannelBootstrap and the tests use for closeForcibly()/close(promise); voidPromise() is a promise nobody observes (docs/transport-porting.md, VoidChannelPromise); promise.setUncancellable() of a write is the CancellationToken check (a cancelled write is released and its Task cancelled, as the Transport's AbstractChannelHandlerContext rejects a cancelled operation). AbstractChannel still owns three pieces, each kept with a CLR comment: the registered flag and the event loop (register(...) checks the re-registration and then runs RegisterAsync, which sets them and fires channelRegistered/channelActive before its Task completes, where Java completes the promise first; EventLoop is the loop of the registration, the parent's); closePromise, which is AbstractChannel's CloseFuture (close(promise, error) runs Java's body and then, at closePromise.setSuccess()/fireChannelInactiveAndDeregister(voidPromise(), wasActive), AbstractChannel's close, which completes CloseFuture and runs channelInactive and, while registered, channelUnregistered in one later event-loop task (invokeLater), or for a never-registered channel AbstractChannel's closeForcibly, which completes CloseFuture without events; DoClose() is empty); and the deregistration (deregister(promise) is AbstractChannel's deregistration, the same invokeLater task with fireChannelInactive false; safeSetSuccess completes the promise from its Task). Measured with scratch probes and the ported tests: a child write completes when its own parent write completes (a write after a pending flow-controlled DATA frame completes first), a write the parent completes at once completes before the write call returns without a flush, a write still pending in the parent stays pending through close and then completes with the parent's outcome, trySetWritable() fires channelWritabilityChanged synchronously, isWritable() is true and bytesBeforeUnwritable() high water mark + 1 after close, and an ExecuteSynchronously continuation of a write Task runs on the thread that completes the parent write. Remaining difference: CloseFuture is AbstractChannel's TaskCompletionSource created with RunContinuationsAsynchronously, so a default-scheduler continuation of it runs asynchronously (a listener on the event-loop scheduler, Http2CodecUtil.AddListener, runs at once on the loop, measured). The constructor takes the parent channel (AbstractChannel's constructor needs it and the id); the anonymous pipeline is a nested DefaultChannelPipeline whose protected internal members are protected overrides; the anonymous visitors and Handle are private nested classes; Http2StreamChannelConfig sets FlowControlledFrameSizeEstimator.INSTANCE in its constructor because getMessageSizeEstimator() is not virtual in the Transport's DefaultChannelConfig, and getOption/setOption are its TryGetValue/SetValue dispatch. The ReadStatus switch is an if/else chain; Queue<Object> (ArrayDeque) is Queue<object>; IOException includes SocketException as in AbstractChannel's write-error handling; new ClosedChannelException().initCause(cause) is a private nested subclass using the Transport type's protected cause constructor (src/Netty.NET.Transport/Channels/ClosedChannelException.cs); "Message must be an " + simpleClassName(Http2StreamFrame) names IHttp2StreamFrame.

stream(Http2FrameStream) returns AbstractHttp2StreamFrame (virtual, overridden covariantly by the subclasses) and IHttp2StreamFrame.Stream is implemented explicitly with it (owner decision 2026-11-19; docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations). The abstract class declares the abstract Name() of Http2Frame, because a C# class must map every interface member. equals/hashCode are Equals/GetHashCode; stream == other.stream() is ReferenceEquals.

Public abstract self-typed builder AbstractInboundHttp2ToHttpAdapterBuilder<T, B> where T : InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter where B : AbstractInboundHttp2ToHttpAdapterBuilder<T, B>; self() casts through object (the unchecked cast), as the base group's AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder. The protected non-final getters and setters (Connection(), MaxContentLength()/MaxContentLength(int), IsValidateHttpHeaders()/ValidateHttpHeaders(bool), IsPropagateSettings()/PropagateSettings(bool), Build()) are protected virtual Java-named methods, because a Java subclass widens them with @Override and a C# override "can't change the accessibility of the virtual method"; the protected final Self() is non-virtual. catch (Throwable) is catch (Exception) and IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException (docs/codec-base-porting.md); the abstract build(...) "throws Exception" has no checked-exception counterpart.

DefaultHeaders<CharSequence, V, CharSequenceMap<V>> is the codec-base DefaultHeaders<ICharSequence, V, CharSequenceMap<V>>, whose value type is a reference type (V : class); ValueConverter is IValueConverter, UnsupportedValueConverter.<V>instance() is UnsupportedValueConverter<V>.Instance() and NameValidator.NOT_NULL is DefaultHeaders.INameValidator<ICharSequence>.NOT_NULL (no unchecked cast).

Public sealed class (the Java class is final) deriving from codec-base's ByteToMessageDecoder; decode(ctx, in, List<Object> out) is Decode(ctx, ByteBuf @in, IList<object> @out) and handlerAdded the HandlerAdded override (docs/codec-base-porting.md). ChannelHandler is IChannelHandler and checkNotNull's NullPointerException is ArgumentNullException. CONNECTION_PREFACE keeps Java's unreleasableBuffer(connectionPrefaceBuf()).asReadOnly() (Unpooled.UnreleasableBuffer/AsReadOnly), and ByteBufUtil.equals(a, aStart, b, bStart, length) is ByteBufUtil.Equals with the same arguments, so the preface peek compares the same octets. ctx.pipeline()/name() are the Pipeline/Name properties and pipeline().remove(handler) returns the pipeline as in Java (docs/transport-porting.md, Decisions). PriorKnowledgeUpgradeEvent is a public sealed nested class with a private constructor; its INSTANCE, private in Java and read by the enclosing class, is internal because C# does not open a nested class's private members to the enclosing class (docs/handler-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations, Access and names). The checked "throws" clauses have no counterpart.

Public class over DecoratingHttp2ConnectionEncoder; the three public static final ints are const. ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource and ChannelFuture is Task; the Write*Async overrides return the promise's Task (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations, as the base group's encoders). WriteDataAsync and both WriteHeadersAsync overloads override the decorator's virtual members; promise.setSuccess() is SetResult(), tryFailure is TrySetException and ctx.newPromise() Http2CodecUtil.NewPromise(). PromiseCombiner is a list of the buffer promises' Tasks, and combiner.finish(promise) is codec-base's CLR-only internal ExecutorPromiseCombiner (src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec/ExecutorPromiseCombiner.cs), which counts the completions on ctx.Executor through Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler and completes the promise with the outcome of Task.WhenAll when the last one completes, as new PromiseCombiner(ctx.executor()) does on its executor (docs/common-task-composition.md, Executor affinity of a combined write). The buffer promises come from Http2CodecUtil.NewPromise() (no RunContinuationsAsynchronously), so the former Task.WhenAll + Http2CodecUtil.Cascade already completed on the event loop; the shared helper keeps one rule across the codecs. The two identical anonymous Http2ConnectionAdapter instances of the constructors are one private nested StreamRemovedListener. CompressionOptions is codec-compression's ICompressionOptions (params ICompressionOptions[]), and the option/encoder types are the codec-compression ports; EmbeddedChannel.builder() is new EmbeddedChannel.Builder() (docs/codec-http-porting.md). zstd-jni is library-not-ported (owner decision 2026-11-23, docs/codec-compression-porting.md: the BCL ZstandardStream/Encoder/Decoder exist only from .NET 11 and the solution stays on .NET 10), so ZstdOptions, Zstd, ZstdEncoder and ZstdDecoder have no C# type and the code behaves as Java does when Zstd.isAvailable() is false, as codec-http's HttpContentCompressor/HttpContentDecompressor do. defaultCompressionOptions() never adds StandardCompressionOptions.zstd(), the instanceof ZstdOptions branch has no type to test, zstdOptions is an always-null ICompressionOptions and the zstd branch of newContentCompressor is unreachable (it throws NotSupportedException). brotli4j is not ported either: Brotli.IsAvailable() is always true and BrotliOptions.parameters() (brotli4j Encoder.Parameters) is not ported, so the encoder is new BrotliEncoder(BrotliOptions) (docs/codec-compression-porting.md). The @Deprecated constructor (delegate, int, int, int) has no @deprecated text and names no replacement, so it is ported with [Obsolete] (owner decision 2026-11-16); a window size or memory level other than 15/8 makes ZlibCodecFactory.NewZlibEncoder throw NotSupportedException (jzlib is not ported). CompressionOptions.class.getSimpleName() is nameof(ICompressionOptions), as codec-http's HttpContentCompressor. The package-private cleanup(...) is internal. Throwable is Exception and IllegalArgumentException ArgumentException. No byte arithmetic.

Public class implementing IHttp2ConnectionDecoder by delegation. The overridable (public, non-final) Java methods are virtual. (the empty-DATA and max-RST decoders override frameListener). The field and parameter delegate are @delegate; List<Object> out is IList<object> @out (docs/codec-base-porting.md) and Closeable.close() is Close(), which the interface's IDisposable.Dispose() calls (docs/handler-porting.md).

Public class over h4's DecoratingHttp2FrameWriter implementing IHttp2ConnectionEncoder and IHttp2SettingsReceivedConsumer. The overridable (public, non-final) Java methods are virtual. (Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder, Http2MaxRstFrameLimitEncoder and StreamBufferingEncoder override lifecycleManager and the writes). The field and parameter delegate are @delegate (a C# keyword). Http2SettingsReceivedConsumer.class in the IllegalStateException (InvalidOperationException) message is typeof(IHttp2SettingsReceivedConsumer), whose ToString() is the full type name where Java's Class.toString() prints "interface " and the class name.

Public class over IHttp2FrameWriter that forwards every call. delegate is a C# keyword, so the field and the constructor parameter are @delegate. ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource and ChannelFuture is Task; the Task-returning methods take the Async suffix (WriteDataAsync, WriteHeadersAsync, WritePriorityAsync, WriteRstStreamAsync, WriteSettingsAsync, WriteSettingsAckAsync, WritePingAsync, WritePushPromiseAsync, WriteGoAwayAsync, WriteWindowUpdateAsync, WriteFrameAsync) and return the promise's Task (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations; owner rule 2). The overridable (public, non-final) Java methods are virtual, so subclasses override them as in Java. configuration() returns IHttp2FrameWriter.IConfiguration; Closeable.close() is Close() and IDisposable.Dispose() comes from the IHttp2FrameWriter default member (docs/handler-porting.md: "Closeable keeps close() as Close() and implements IDisposable.Dispose() with it").

IntObjectMap<Http2Stream>/IntObjectHashMap are Dictionary<int, IHttp2Stream> (owner decision 2026-11-19, confirmed 2026-11-25); streamMap.get(id) is GetValueOrDefault. The inner (non-static) classes and the anonymous classes, which are private nested classes, receive the enclosing instance explicitly, because a C# nested class has no enclosing instance. The nested ConnectionStream class is ConnectionStream_, because it cannot share the name of the connectionStream() method (CS0102, owner rule: trailing underscore); state() of the streams is State_() (IHttp2Stream). close(Promise<Void>) is CloseAsync(TaskCompletionSource) returning the promise's Task; PromiseNotifier.cascade(closePromise, promise) is a synchronous continuation of closePromise that copies its outcome with TrySetFromTask (docs/common-task-composition.md, PromiseNotifier), without the cascade's back propagation of a cancelled promise; the branch that replaces a void closePromise is left out because there is no void promise (docs/transport-porting.md: VoidChannelPromise). The Iterator of close() is the Dictionary enumerator: Iterator.remove() is Dictionary.Remove of the current key, which "may be safely called without invalidating active enumerators" (.NET Core 3.0+), so close(Iterator)/deactivate/removeFromActiveStreams/removeStream take the enumerator only as the marker that the removal happens during that iteration. The wildcard DefaultEndpoint<?>/DefaultEndpoint<? extends Http2FlowController> is a non-generic abstract DefaultEndpoint base with every member that does not use F, and DefaultEndpoint<F> adds the flow controller (as IHttp2Connection splits IEndpoint/IEndpoint<F>); createStream/reservePushStream narrow their return type to DefaultStream in Java, so the public methods return DefaultStream and the IEndpoint members are implemented explicitly. The package-private nested Event interface is the internal IEvent and its anonymous implementations the private nested ActivateEvent/DeactivateEvent; the anonymous Http2StreamVisitor of closeStreamsGreaterThanLastKnownStreamId is CloseStreamsGreaterThanVisitor. java.util.LinkedHashSet is Common's LinkedHashSet and ArrayDeque is Queue. A Java switch on the State enum class is an if/else chain on reference equality (see IHttp2Stream.State; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/builtin-types/enum). Arrays.copyOf is Array.Resize. Java's unchecked (V) casts of the stream properties are erased and cannot fail; the C# PropertyMap gives default(V) for a missing value or a value of another type (measured: the local flow controller replaces a ReducedFlowState with a DefaultState through setProperty, whose previous value Java casts unchecked to the new type). equals() is reference equality (super.equals) and System.identityHashCode is RuntimeHelpers.GetHashCode; getClass().getSimpleName() is GetType().Name. Throwable is Exception and the "Caught Throwable ..." log texts are kept; numbers concatenated into messages use the invariant culture.

Public class implementing IHttp2ConnectionDecoder. The overridable (public, non-final) Java methods are virtual. calculateMaxHeaderListSizeGoAway is protected virtual and onGoAwayRead0 (package-private) internal. The @Deprecated constructor with autoAckPing has no @deprecated text and so no named replacement; it is ported with [Obsolete] (owner decision 2026-11-16), and the constructor that delegates to it, as in Java, suppresses CS0612 locally. The inner classes FrameReadListener and PrefaceFrameListener receive the enclosing decoder in their constructors, so the field initializer of internalFrameListener runs in the constructor (CS0236). A Java switch on Http2Stream.State is an if/else chain on reference equality (State is an enum class and a C# case label must be a constant); state() is State_() (CS0102 with the nested State type). Endpoint<?> is the non-generic IHttp2Connection.IEndpoint. ctx.newSucceededFuture() is Task.CompletedTask and ctx.newPromise() Http2CodecUtil.NewPromise() (the Task of the auto-ack SETTINGS/PING writes is discarded, as Java discards the future). catch (Http2Exception | RuntimeException e) is catch (Exception) because every CLR exception is unchecked; catch (IllegalArgumentException) is catch (ArgumentException), which codec-http's HttpUtil.NormalizeAndGetContentLength throws for every invalid content-length (Java's NumberFormatException is an IllegalArgumentException; the C# helper wraps its FormatException). List<? extends CharSequence> is IList<ICharSequence>, Iterator<Entry<...>> the codec-base IIterator<IEntry<...>>, Class equality is Type equality and Http2SettingsReceivedConsumer.class in the message is typeof(IHttp2SettingsReceivedConsumer). Messages are Java format strings (Http2CodecUtil.Format).

Public class implementing IHttp2ConnectionEncoder and IHttp2SettingsReceivedConsumer. ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource and ChannelFuture is Task; the Task-returning methods take the Async suffix and return the promise's Task (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations; owner rule 2); promise.unvoid() is the promise itself (there is no void promise, docs/transport-porting.md), setFailure/tryFailure are SetException/TrySetException followed by returning the Task, future.cause() is Http2CodecUtil.Cause and future.addListener(...) is Http2CodecUtil.AddListener (a continuation on Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor, DefaultPromise's listener timing). The overridable (public, non-final) Java methods are virtual. A Java switch on Http2Stream.State is an if/else chain on reference equality (State is an enum class and a C# case label must be a constant); state() is State_() (CS0102 with the nested State type). The inner (non-static) classes OutstandingLocalSettings, FlowControlledData, FlowControlledHeaders and the public abstract FlowControlledBase receive the enclosing encoder in their constructors (internal; Java's is package-private); FlowControlledBase declares abstract the FlowControlled members Java leaves to the subclasses (a C# class must map every interface member) and its ChannelFutureListener.operationComplete is OperationComplete(Task). ArrayDeque<OutstandingLocalSettings> is a LinkedList because operationComplete removes an arbitrary element (Queue<T> has no Remove(T)); poll() removes the first node; the remote-settings ArrayDeque is a Queue (TryDequeue). FlowControlledData creates its Transport CoalescingBufferQueue for ctx.Channel, because Java uses promise.channel() and a TaskCompletionSource has no channel; ctx.newPromise().addListener(this) is Http2CodecUtil.NewPromise() plus AddListener, ctx.write(msg, promise) is Http2CodecUtil.Write, and the nested writePromise of the empty-data branch is emptyWritePromise (a nested local cannot reuse the enclosing name, CS0136). SimpleChannelPromiseAggregator.newPromise() returns child promises and doneAllocatingPromises() the aggregate (see Http2CodecUtil). FlowControlledData.class != next.getClass() is a Type comparison. HttpStatusClass.valueOf(headers.status()) == INFORMATIONAL is a reference comparison of the codec-http HttpStatusClass instances. IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException, IllegalArgumentException ArgumentException and UnsupportedOperationException NotSupportedException; stream ids and booleans in messages keep their Java text (Http2CodecUtil.ToJavaString).

ByteBufHolder is IByteBufHolder: content() and refCnt() are the Content and RefCnt properties (docs/buffer-porting.md, Buffer holders and conversion). stream(Http2FrameStream) narrows its return type; it is a C# 9 covariant override of the virtual AbstractHttp2StreamFrame.Stream(IHttp2FrameStream), which implements IHttp2StreamFrame.Stream explicitly (owner decision 2026-11-19: narrowing re-declarations are inherited; docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations). copy/duplicate/retainedDuplicate/replace/retain/touch return DefaultHttp2DataFrame and the IByteBufHolder/IReferenceCounted members declared with other return types are implemented explicitly with them. IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException. toString() keeps Java's text: a null stream prints "null", numbers use the invariant culture and booleans print true/false (Http2CodecUtil.ToJavaString, String.valueOf).

Public class implementing IHttp2FrameReader, IHttp2FrameSizePolicy and IHttp2FrameReader.IConfiguration. The inner (non-static) classes HeadersContinuation and HeadersBlockBuilder get the reader as a constructor argument (a C# nested class has no implicit outer instance) and reach its fields through it; HeadersBlockBuilder stays a protected nested class with an internal constructor, because the reader creates it. The three anonymous HeadersContinuation subclasses of readHeadersFrame/readPushPromiseFrame are the private nested PriorityHeadersContinuation, HeadersContinuationWithoutPriority and PushPromiseHeadersContinuation, which receive the values the Java closures capture. The frame type is a System.Byte: the switches over it and the listener calls use the unsigned octet, while the three exception messages that format the frame type with %s pass it as sbyte, so a type 0x80-0xFF prints the negative Java value (byte-sign spot). readUnsignedByte() is the unsigned ReadByte(), readUnsignedInt() returns uint (widened to long as in Java), writerIndex(int) is the WriterIndex property. In readFrame, catch (RuntimeException) and catch (Throwable) are one catch (Exception) because both are CLR Exceptions; it sets readError and rethrows with throw; (PlatformDependent.throwException keeps the original exception). Http2Settings.put(id, Long.valueOf(value)) is Put(char, long) and its IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException, whose Message is Java's getMessage() text. Exception messages keep the Java format strings through Http2Exception (Http2CodecUtil.Format). The overridable (public, non-final) Java methods are virtual, so subclasses override them as in Java.

Public class implementing IHttp2FrameWriter, IHttp2FrameSizePolicy and IHttp2FrameWriter.IConfiguration. ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource and ChannelFuture is Task; the Task-returning methods take the Async suffix (WriteDataAsync, WriteHeadersAsync, WritePriorityAsync, WriteRstStreamAsync, WriteSettingsAsync, WriteSettingsAckAsync, WritePingAsync, WritePushPromiseAsync, WriteGoAwayAsync, WriteWindowUpdateAsync, WriteFrameAsync) and return the promise's Task (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations; owner rule 2). ctx.write(msg, promise) is Http2CodecUtil.Write, which completes the promise from the context's write Task (TrySetFromTask, the PromiseNotifier mapping of docs/common-task-composition.md); promise.setFailure(t) returning the promise is SetException(t) followed by the promise's Task. SimpleChannelPromiseAggregator (Http2CodecUtil) hands out child promises from NewPromise() and is returned through its Task. ZERO_BUFFER is LeakPresenceDetector.StaticInitializer over an unreleasable read-only direct buffer, as in Java. "headersEncoder instanceof Closeable" is a test for IDisposable (the Closeable mapping of docs/handler-porting.md; DefaultHttp2HeadersEncoder implements it), and new RuntimeException(e) keeps Java's detail message cause.toString() through Common's ThrowableUtil.ThrowableToString (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Exceptions). PlatformDependent.throwException(t) is throw; after the aggregator is failed. Http2Settings is a Dictionary<char, long>, so the SETTINGS entries are written in Dictionary (insertion) order where Java writes CharObjectHashMap's hash-slot order (owner decision 2026-11-25; a SETTINGS frame holds each identifier once); entry.value().intValue() is the unchecked int conversion. (int) (0x80000000L | streamDependency) is computed with an explicit long conversion of the verified non-negative dependency (no sign-extension warning, CS0675) and an unchecked narrowing, giving Java's value. checkPositive/checkPositiveOrZero are the ObjectUtil methods (ArgumentException). The overridable (public, non-final) Java methods are virtual, so subclasses override them as in Java.

DefaultByteBufHolder is the Buffer port's DefaultByteBufHolder; the overrides that narrow its return types to Http2GoAwayFrame are C# 9 covariant overrides returning IHttp2GoAwayFrame (as codec-smtp DefaultSmtpContent), and content() is the Content property (docs/buffer-porting.md). The package-private constructor is internal; errorCode >>> 32 is the C# unsigned shift. toString() keeps Java's text: a null stream prints "null", numbers use the invariant culture and booleans print true/false (Http2CodecUtil.ToJavaString, String.valueOf).

DefaultHeaders<CharSequence, CharSequence, Http2Headers> is the codec-base DefaultHeaders<ICharSequence, ICharSequence, IHttp2Headers> and the class implements IHttp2Headers; HashingStrategy is IEqualityComparer and AsciiString.CASE_SENSITIVE_HASHER/CASE_INSENSITIVE_HASHER are the Common comparers (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Headers). NameValidator/ValueValidator are DefaultHeaders.INameValidator/IValueValidator<ICharSequence>, whose NOT_NULL/NO_VALIDATION constants need no unchecked cast; the anonymous validators are the private nested Http2NameValidator/Http2ValueValidator and the anonymous ByteProcessor is a Func<byte, bool>. PlatformDependent.throwException(connectionError(...)) throws the checked Http2Exception without declaring it; C# has no checked exceptions, so it is a throw statement (catch (Http2Exception) { throw; }) and the unreachable return after it is left out. The inner class Http2HeaderEntry, which reads the enclosing instance's firstNonPseudo and head, takes the DefaultHttp2Headers in its constructor; the field initializer firstNonPseudo = head is an assignment in the constructor (CS0236: "A field initializer cannot reference the non-static field"). The protected codec-base members (ValidateName, ValidateValue, NewHeaderEntry) are overridden as protected (protected internal in another assembly); HeaderEntry.Remove is overridden as protected internal, because codec-base opens its internals to this assembly (InternalsVisibleTo, for ExecutorPromiseCombiner) and an override of a protected internal member it can see keeps both modifiers (CS0507). The non-final methods are virtual; equals/hashCode are Equals/GetHashCode with CASE_SENSITIVE_HASHER. Integer.toHexString and the index of the value validator message use the invariant culture. defaultHtt2NameValidator() keeps its Java spelling (DefaultHtt2NameValidator()).

Configuration is IHttp2HeadersDecoder.IConfiguration. The package-private constructor taking the package-private HpackDecoder is internal. The public members and the protected non-final validateHeaderValues()/newHeaders() are virtual, the protected final numberOfHeadersGuess()/validateHeaders() are not (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Cookie and CORS). The @Deprecated annotation on the initialHuffmanDecodeCapacity parameter has no C# counterpart for a parameter; the constructor itself is not deprecated and its Javadoc says "Does nothing, do not use". catch (Http2Exception e) { throw e; } is a rethrow (throw;), catch (Throwable) is catch (Exception) and getMessage() is Message. The moving average keeps single-precision float arithmetic.

Closeable is IDisposable with close() kept as Close() and IDisposable.Dispose() calling it (docs/handler-porting.md: "Closeable keeps close() as Close() and implements IDisposable.Dispose() with it"); DefaultHttp2FrameWriter tests "is IDisposable" where Java tests "instanceof Closeable". Configuration and SensitivityDetector are the I-prefixed nested interfaces of IHttp2HeadersEncoder; the interface constant NEVER_SENSITIVE is reached through the interface name. The package-private constructor taking the package-private HpackEncoder is internal. The public members of the non-final class are virtual (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Cookie and CORS). catch (Http2Exception e) { throw e; } is a rethrow (throw;), catch (Throwable) is catch (Exception) and getMessage() is Message.

stream(Http2FrameStream) narrows its return type; it is a C# 9 covariant override of the virtual AbstractHttp2StreamFrame.Stream(IHttp2FrameStream), which implements IHttp2StreamFrame.Stream explicitly (owner decision 2026-11-19: narrowing re-declarations are inherited; docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations). toString() keeps Java's text: a null stream prints "null", numbers use the invariant culture and booleans print true/false (Http2CodecUtil.ToJavaString, String.valueOf).

The inner (non-static) classes and the anonymous classes, which are private nested classes, receive the enclosing instance explicitly, because a C# nested class has no enclosing instance. Double.compare(ratio, 0.0)/(ratio, 1.0) is double.CompareTo: Java orders NaN above every value and .NET below, but a NaN ratio fails one of the two range checks in both, and -0.0 fails the first in both. review.scope: Public class over Http2FrameListenerDecorator (its listener field is protected internal readonly). The inner class ConsumedBytesConverter (IHttp2LocalFlowController) receives the enclosing listener; the anonymous Http2ConnectionAdapter is the nested StreamRemovedListener and the anonymous ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter of Http2Decompressor is its nested DecompressorHandler, which reads and writes the decompressor's private fields. The package-private decompressor(stream) returns the private Http2Decompressor and is private ("The return type and parameter types of a method shall be at least as accessible as the method itself", C# specification, Accessibility constraints). zstd-jni is library-not-ported (owner decision 2026-11-23, docs/codec-compression-porting.md: the BCL ZstandardStream/Encoder/Decoder exist only from .NET 11 and the solution stays on .NET 10), so ZstdOptions, Zstd, ZstdEncoder and ZstdDecoder have no C# type and the code behaves as Java does when Zstd.isAvailable() is false, as codec-http's HttpContentCompressor/HttpContentDecompressor do. The "Zstd.isAvailable() && ZSTD" branch is left out, so a "zstd" content-encoding is passed through undecoded. Brotli.IsAvailable() is always true; new BrotliDecoder(maxAllocation) keeps the Java call, which passes maxAllocation as the input buffer size (0 selects the default). java.nio.channels.ClosedChannelException is the Transport ClosedChannelException; EmbeddedChannel rethrows a recorded handler exception unchanged (ExceptionDispatchInfo in CheckException), so "t instanceof Http2Exception" sees the listener's exception as in Java. assert is Debug.Assert, Math.ceil Math.Ceiling (the int conversion saturates in both), catch (Http2Exception e) { throw e; } is "throw;". The two @Deprecated constructors whose @deprecated texts name the (..., int maxAllocation) overloads are not ported. Measured (DataCompressionHttp2Test.encodingTooBigMessage, 512 KiB input, maxAllocation 64 KiB): gzip rejects with a StreamException whose root cause is DecompressionException("Decompression buffer has reached maximum size: 65536"), brotli delivers chunks of at most 65536 bytes and snappy of at most 32767 bytes.

EmptyHeaders<CharSequence, CharSequence, Http2Headers> is the codec-base EmptyHeaders<ICharSequence, ICharSequence, IHttp2Headers>. The pseudo-header setters narrow the return type to EmptyHttp2Headers; C# 9 covariant returns cover class overrides only, so the public methods return EmptyHttp2Headers and the IHttp2Headers members are implemented explicitly with them (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations). UnsupportedOperationException is NotSupportedException.

Package-private final class -> internal sealed class with internal constructors and package-private members (decode, setMaxHeaderTableSize, setMaxHeaderListSize, the getters, the test hooks and the static decodeULE128 overloads). The static exceptions are Http2Exception.NewStatic with typeof(HpackDecoder). The byte that decode(ByteBuf, Http2HeadersSink) reads for each header representation is read as sbyte, because "b < 0" tests the sign of the Java byte (the indexed-header bit); the masks give the same values for the signed and the unsigned byte. decodeDynamicTableSizeUpdates and decodeULE128 only mask or compare with non-negative constants, so System.Byte gives the Java results. The simple enums IndexType and HeaderType are C# enums, a null HeaderType is HeaderType?. The last section of each nested switch ends with break (C# forbids falling out of a switch section, CS8070) and the READ_INDEXED_HEADER section is a block, because a C# local is scoped to the whole switch block and the nested switch declares a local of the same name (CS0136). throw new Error(...) is UnreachableException and IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException; catch (IllegalArgumentException) of Http2HeadersSink leaves out ArgumentNullException and ArgumentOutOfRangeException, which derive from ArgumentException in the BCL but stand for Java's NullPointerException/IndexOutOfBoundsException (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Multipart: HttpPostBodyUtil.IsIllegalArgument). getMessage() is Message; readerIndex/writerIndex/readableBytes are the ByteBuf properties; HttpHeaderValidationUtil is the codec-http port.

Package-private final class -> internal sealed class; the package-private fields hpackHeaderFields/head/tail and the constructor are internal. IndexOutOfBoundsException is ArgumentOutOfRangeException (created with a null parameter name so that Message is the Java text) and IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException (docs/codec-base-porting.md); numbers in messages use the invariant culture.

Package-private final class -> internal sealed class with internal constructors, constants and the test hooks length()/size()/getHeaderField(int). Http2Headers is IEnumerable<IEntry<ICharSequence, ICharSequence>>, so the for-each over Map.Entry is a foreach over codec-base IEntry (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Headers). SensitivityDetector is IHttp2HeadersEncoder.ISensitivityDetector. The field initializer latest = head reads an instance field, which a C# field initializer cannot do (CS0236), so the constructor assigns it. IndexType is switched as a C# enum and throw new Error(...) is UnreachableException; assert is Debug.Assert. out.writeBytes(array, offset, length) of an AsciiString writes the span of its backing array; out.writeCharSequence(string, ISO_8859_1) takes the ByteBufUtil.writeAscii path in Java (AbstractByteBuf.setCharSequence0 for US_ASCII and ISO_8859_1), so it is ByteBufUtil.WriteAscii, which writes AsciiString.c2b of each char (docs/codec-http-porting.md: writeCharSequence(..., US_ASCII) is ByteBufUtil.WriteAscii); HpackEncoderTest.testSanitization checks the "?" for chars above 0xFF. hashMask is a byte below 128 (the array length is at most 128), so the Java byte and System.Byte masks are equal; the non-negative mask of encodeInteger is OR-ed into the long as uint (CS0675). Math.max/min are Math.Max/Min.

Package-private class -> internal class; the package-private constant, static sizeOf, fields name/value (internal readonly ICharSequence), constructor and size() are internal (the tests and HpackEncoder.NameValueEntry use them). CharSequence is ICharSequence; checkNotNull is ObjectUtil.CheckNotNull (ArgumentNullException); toString() concatenates the CharSequence texts.

Package-private final class -> internal sealed class. It implements ByteProcessor in Java; ByteProcessor is the Common Func<byte, bool> (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations): the processor keeps process(byte) as Process(byte) and the forEachByte call receives a delegate to it that is created once. The 4096-row HUFFS table is copied with every comment; the byte flag constants are const byte and the table expressions combine them as int, as Java widens them. input >> 4 of the Java (signed) byte and of the System.Byte differ only above the low nibble, which processNibble masks away (input & 0x0F); (byte) state keeps the low eight bits in both. BAD_ENCODING is Http2Exception.NewStatic(..., typeof(HpackHuffmanDecoder), ...); the readerIndex accessors are the ByteBuf ReaderIndex property.

Package-private final class -> internal sealed class. ByteProcessor is the Common Func<byte, bool> (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations): the processor keeps process(byte) as Process(byte) and the forEachByte call receives a delegate to it that is created once. The inner (non-static) EncodeProcessor/EncodedLengthProcessor read codes and lengths of the encoder, so they receive it in their constructor (a C# nested class has no enclosing instance). The catch (Exception e) { PlatformDependent.throwException(e); } blocks only satisfied Java's checked ByteProcessor.process(...) throws Exception and are left out (the processors throw nothing; handler's SslHandler maps throwException to a plain rethrow, docs/handler-porting.md). AsciiString.c2b is AsciiString.C2b. The codes (below 2^30) and the EOS padding bits are non-negative and are OR-ed into the long as uint (zero extension, avoiding the C# sign-extension warning CS0675), which gives the value of Java's int-to-long widening; the Java byte value & 0xFF and the System.Byte value are the same table index.

Package-private final class -> internal sealed class with internal members. Arrays.asList(...) of the 61 entries is an array behind IReadOnlyList (size() is Count, get(i) the indexer). The two static initializer blocks are the private InitHeaderNames() and InitHeadersWithNonEmptyValues(), which the static constructor runs in the Java order: a class has only one static constructor, and the static field initializers "run in the textual order in which they appear in the class declaration. The initializers run immediately before the static constructor". HEADER_NAMES_TABLE_SHIFT and HEADERS_WITH_NON_EMPTY_VALUES_TABLE_SHIFT depend on the static readonly PlatformDependent.BIG_ENDIAN_NATIVE_ORDER, so they are static readonly instead of constants. AsciiString.hashCode(CharSequence) is the Common AsciiString.HashCode, which keeps Java's hashing (PlatformDependent.HashCodeAscii), so each bucket holds one entry as in Java (the static constructor throws InvalidOperationException on a collision; HpackStaticTableTest exercises all lookups). The String names and values of the table are AsciiString.Cached values as in Java; HttpHeaderNames/HttpMethod/HttpResponseStatus come from codec-http. The fields of the private nested HeaderNameIndex/HeaderIndex are internal readonly.

Package-private final class -> internal sealed class with internal static members; the private constructor keeps its "// utility class" comment, so it is a class, not a static class. equalsConstantTime/equalsVariableTime use the Common ports: AsciiString.array()/arrayOffset() are Array()/ArrayOffset() (the backing array, no copy), PlatformDependent.EqualsConstantTime and ConstantTimeUtils.EqualsConstantTime(ICharSequence, ICharSequence), AsciiString.contentEquals is the static AsciiString.ContentEquals. The simple enum IndexType is a C# enum. HUFFMAN_CODE_LENGTHS holds code lengths 5..30, so the Java byte[] and the C# byte[] values are equal; HUFFMAN_EOS is a const.

IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException and IllegalArgumentException ArgumentException (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Exceptions); pipeline().context(Class) is Context(Type) (docs/transport-porting.md, Interfaces added); getSimpleName()/simpleClassName are StringUtil.SimpleClassName(Type). The checked throws clauses have no counterpart.

Public class implementing codec-http's HttpClientUpgradeHandler.IUpgradeCodec (owner rule: I prefix; src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http/HttpClientUpgradeHandler.cs). CharSequence is ICharSequence, Collection<CharSequence> ICollection<ICharSequence> and Collections.singletonList a ReadOnlyCollection<ICharSequence> over one element (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations); the String header value that getSettingsHeaderValue returns as a CharSequence is wrapped in StringCharSequence. The seven constructors keep their Java overloads and casts ((String) null, (Http2ConnectionHandler) frameCodec); checkNotNull's NullPointerException is ArgumentNullException (docs/codec-base-porting.md). getSettingsHeaderValue: Http2Settings is a Dictionary<char, long> (owner decision 2026-11-19, confirmed 2026-11-25; src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2/Http2Settings.cs), so CharObjectMap.PrimitiveEntry<Long> is KeyValuePair<char, long> and the entries enumerate in insertion order, where Java's CharObjectHashMap walks its slots (hashCode(key) & mask) from index 0 upward (https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/64cc10f38ea5f5bd7eae48507817c66680d0afdc/common/src/main/templates/io/netty/util/collection/KObjectHashMap.template). Measured for the default client settings (Http2FrameCodecBuilder.forClient().build()): the port writes the entries in the order 4, 3, 1, 5, 6, 2 (header "AAQAAP__AAMAAABkAAEAABAAAAUAAEAAAAYAACAAAAIAAAAB") where Java writes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 ("AAEAABAAAAIAAAABAAMAAABkAAQAAP__AAUAAEAAAAYAACAA"): the same six settings with the same values, which a receiver applies identically because the keys are distinct; no test compares the header bytes. entry.value().intValue() is the unchecked (int) cast: Long.intValue() is "a narrowing primitive conversion" (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/Long.html) and the C# cast likewise truncates by discarding the most significant bits (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/builtin-types/numeric-conversions). Base64.encode(buf, URL_SAFE) is the codec-base port (src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec/Base64Codec/Base64.cs), toString(UTF_8) is ToString(Encoding.UTF8) and ReferenceCountUtil.release(null) returns false as in Java. ctx.pipeline()/name() are the Pipeline/Name properties (docs/transport-porting.md, Decisions) and ctx.close() discards the returned Task (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Outbound operations). The public non-final interface methods are virtual; the checked "throws" clauses have no counterpart.

The final class with a private constructor is a static class; the primitive constants are const (char settings identifiers are (char) casts of the Java char literals 1..8), and the String constants typed CharSequence (HTTP_UPGRADE_PROTOCOL_NAME, TLS_UPGRADE_PROTOCOL_NAME) are StringCharSequence values because a C# string is not an ICharSequence (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations). CONNECTION_PREFACE keeps LeakPresenceDetector.staticInitializer/unreleasableBuffer/directBuffer/asReadOnly with the Common/Buffer ports (as codec-http HttpObjectEncoder); "...".getBytes(UTF_8) is Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes. MILLISECONDS.convert(30, SECONDS) is TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30) in milliseconds (static readonly). Throwable.getCause() is InnerException; getMessage() is Message, never null in .NET, so the null check of toByteBuf keeps its Java shape only and an exception created without a message gives the CLR default text as GOAWAY debug data where Java sends an empty buffer (docs/codec-http-porting.md, codec-http Utf8FrameValidator). StreamByteDistributor.StreamState is IStreamByteDistributor.IStreamState. SimpleChannelPromiseAggregator extends DefaultChannelPromise; it derives from TaskCompletionSource, whose completion methods are not virtual, so the overridden setSuccess/trySuccess/setFailure/tryFailure are the class's own SetSuccess/TrySuccess/SetFailure/TryFailure and newPromise() returns a new child TaskCompletionSource whose synchronous continuation calls TrySuccess()/TryFailure(cause) (what Java's channel does with the aggregator it was given); doneAllocatingPromises() returns the aggregate promise. String.format is the CLR-only internal Format, which keeps the Java text of %d/%s/%b/%% (Formatter: %s of null is "null", %b of null is "false"; the integers use the invariant culture). CLR-only internal helpers of the package, each with a CLR comment: ToJavaString (String.valueOf text: "null", true/false, invariant numbers), NewPromise (ctx.newPromise()/voidPromise(): a TaskCompletionSource without RunContinuationsAsynchronously, as codec-http's handshakers), Write/WriteAndFlush/Close (ctx.write/writeAndFlush/close with a promise: TrySetFromTask, the PromiseNotifier mapping of docs/common-task-composition.md), Cascade, AddListener (future.addListener: a continuation on Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor, the DefaultPromise.notifyListeners timing; docs/codec-http-porting.md, Listener timing) and Cause (future.cause(): the faulted Task's first inner exception, a TaskCanceledException for a canceled Task). IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException.

The Java interface takes the I prefix (owner rule). The nested interfaces take the I prefix as well. Endpoint<F extends Http2FlowController> is split in two: the wildcard type Endpoint<?>/Endpoint<? extends Http2FlowController> (the result of opposite() and a local of DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder) is the non-generic IEndpoint with every member that does not use F, and IEndpoint<F> : IEndpoint adds flowController() and flowController(F): C# has no wildcard types and IEndpoint<F> cannot be covariant because F is also a parameter type (covariant type parameters "can be used as the return types of the interface's methods"). Future<Void> close(Promise<Void>) is CloseAsync(TaskCompletionSource) returning the promise's Task (docs/common-task-composition.md).

Implements IHttp2Connection.IListener (the nested Listener with the I prefix) with empty bodies; the non-final Java methods are public virtual so that the flow controllers, the distributors and the users override them.

The Java interface takes the I prefix (owner rule). Closeable is IDisposable: Close() stays the Java member and the interface implements IDisposable.Dispose() with it (docs/handler-porting.md: "Closeable keeps close() as Close() and implements IDisposable.Dispose() with it"). List<Object> out is IList<object> @out (docs/codec-base-porting.md).

The Java interface takes the I prefix (owner rule). writeFrame(...) is re-declared in Java only to document it and has the signature of IHttp2FrameWriter.WriteFrameAsync, so its comment stays and the member is inherited (a repeated interface member would hide it, CS0108).

Public class over the codec-base ByteToMessageDecoder implementing IHttp2LifecycleManager and the Transport IChannelOutboundHandler. The outbound operations are the Transport's Task-returning members: bind/connect create the TaskCompletionSource that the private PrefaceSendListener completes after the preface is sent and return its Task; close(ctx, promise) is CloseAsync(ctx, CancellationToken), which returns the Task of its own promise (completed by ClosingChannelFutureListener through Http2CodecUtil.Close; the CancellationToken reaches the context only in the decoupleCloseAndGoAway close); disconnect/deregister/read/write pass to the context with the caller's CancellationToken. ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource and ChannelFuture Task (docs/codec-http-porting.md); ctx.newPromise()/ctx.voidPromise() are Http2CodecUtil.NewPromise, promise.unvoid() is the promise itself (no void promises, docs/transport-porting.md), ctx.newSucceededFuture() is Task.CompletedTask and future.cause() is Http2CodecUtil.Cause. Every ChannelFutureListener is an Action<Task> run through Http2CodecUtil.AddListener, a continuation on Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor (DefaultPromise.notifyListeners timing, docs/codec-http-porting.md Listener timing); closeStream(...) has no context in Java, so the context of handlerAdded is kept in the CLR-only field listenerCtx for that listener (a synchronous continuation before handlerAdded). ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE_ON_FAILURE is the private CloseOnFailure, which closes ctx.Channel (a Task has no channel()). ClosingChannelFutureListener schedules its timeout with ctx.Executor.ScheduleAsync and a CancellationTokenSource (cancel(false) is Cancel(false)), and its long timeout with TimeUnit is a TimeSpan. The switches on Http2Stream.State are if/else chains on reference equality (IHttp2Stream.State is a class with static readonly instances); state() is State_(). The Http2StreamVisitor lambda of hasPendingData() is the private PendingDataVisitor and the anonymous Http2ConnectionAdapter of handlerAdded() the private StreamClosedListener; the inner classes BaseDecoder/PrefaceDecoder/FrameDecoder/PrefaceSendListener receive the handler instance. The protected constructors and onConnectionError(...) are protected internal because the builder and the tests reach them through package access; channelReadComplete0 is internal. getUnsignedByte is GetByte (unsigned octet; the frame type and flags are compared with non-negative constants, so the Java sign plays no role), in.toString(i, n, US_ASCII) is ToString(i, n, Encoding.ASCII) and debugData.toString(UTF_8) ToString(Encoding.UTF8). Throwable is Exception, IllegalArgumentException ArgumentException and IllegalStateException InvalidOperationException; Set<Integer> is HashSet<int>; the long in the gracefulShutdownTimeoutMillis exception text uses Http2CodecUtil.ToJavaString. Http2CodecUtil.toByteBuf of an exception without a message gives the CLR default Message text as GOAWAY debug data where Java sends an empty buffer (getMessage() is never null in .NET).

Public sealed class over AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder<Http2ConnectionHandler, Http2ConnectionHandlerBuilder>. The @Override methods that widen protected members to public are public members declared new that call base (a C# override "can't change the accessibility of the virtual method"); build(...) with the codec arguments is the protected override of the abstract Build and calls the protected internal Http2ConnectionHandler constructor. The @Deprecated initialHuffmanDecodeCapacity(int) has no @deprecated text and is ported with the [Obsolete] text of the member it exposes (owner decision 2026-11-16).
The package-private INSTANCE is internal. No other CLR difference.

The final package-private class with a private constructor is an internal static class. AtomicInteger is an int field updated with Interlocked (getAndIncrement() is Interlocked.Increment - 1, decrementAndGet() Interlocked.Decrement, get() Volatile.Read; docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations). GlobalPropertyKey is an internal sealed nested class whose private constructor is internal, because the enclosing class cannot reach a private member of a nested class in C#; equals/hashCode are Equals/GetHashCode. The count in the "Only N global keys" message uses the invariant culture.

Package-private final class: internal sealed with an internal constructor. ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource and ChannelFuture is Task; the Task-returning methods take the Async suffix and return the promise's Task (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations; owner rule 2); promise.unvoid() is the promise itself (there is no void promise, docs/transport-porting.md), setFailure/tryFailure are SetException/TrySetException followed by returning the Task, future.cause() is Http2CodecUtil.Cause and future.addListener(...) is Http2CodecUtil.AddListener (a continuation on Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.Executor, DefaultPromise's listener timing). The ChannelFutureListener lambda that decrements outstandingControlFrames is an Action<Task> assigned in the constructor (a field initializer cannot reference the instance, CS0236), and promise.unvoid().addListener(listener) attaches it with Http2CodecUtil.AddListener and returns the promise. ctx.close() discards the returned Task; ctx.flush() is Flush().

Public sealed class (the Java class is final) implementing the handler port's IChunkedInput<IHttp2DataFrame> (ChunkedInput<Http2DataFrame>); the wrapped ChunkedInput<ByteBuf> is IChunkedInput<ByteBuf> and Http2FrameStream is IHttp2FrameStream (src/Netty.NET.Handler/Stream/IChunkedInput.cs), as codec-http's HttpChunkedInput. The @Deprecated readChunk(ChannelHandlerContext) override (no Javadoc, no comment) has no counterpart: the interface member it overrides is @Deprecated with the replacement readChunk(ByteBufAllocator) named and is not ported (owner decision 2026-11-16, recorded in IChunkedInput.cs), so callers pass ctx.Alloc() to ReadChunk(IByteBufAllocator). isEndOfInput/close/length/progress are IsEndOfInput/Close/Length/Progress and isEndStream() is IsEndStream(); new DefaultHttp2DataFrame(...).stream(stream) uses the covariant Stream(IHttp2FrameStream) override that returns DefaultHttp2DataFrame. ObjectUtil.checkNotNull is the Common ObjectUtil.CheckNotNull (ArgumentNullException for the NullPointerException, docs/codec-base-porting.md); "throws Exception" has no C# counterpart. No byte value is involved.

The Java interface takes the I prefix (owner rule). Attribute<HttpScheme> is the Common IAttribute<HttpScheme> and AttributeKey.valueOf(HttpScheme.class, "STREAMFRAMECODEC_SCHEME") is AttributeKey<HttpScheme>.ValueOf(Type, string), whose pool name uses Type.FullName (Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http.HttpScheme#STREAMFRAMECODEC_SCHEME) where Java uses Class.getName() (src/Netty.NET.Common/AttributeKey.cs); the key is private, so the name is not observable. ctx.channel(), ch.parent() and ch.pipeline() are the Transport's Channel, Parent and Pipeline properties and pipeline().get(SslHandler.class) is Pipeline.Get<SslHandler>() (docs/transport-porting.md, Decisions), with the handler port's SslHandler on SslStream (docs/handler-porting.md, SSL); Http2StreamChannel is the IHttp2StreamChannel interface (src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2/IHttp2StreamChannel.cs). Status text concatenation uses HttpResponseStatus.ToString(), which keeps Java's "100 Continue" text. "throws Exception" and "throws Http2Exception" have no C# counterpart. The status checks compare UTF-16 chars of the :status value, so no byte sign is involved.
The Java interface takes the I prefix (owner rule). No other CLR difference.

The Java interface takes the I prefix (owner rule). ByteBufHolder is IByteBufHolder, whose content() is the read-only Content property (docs/buffer-porting.md, Buffer holders and conversion); copy/duplicate/retainedDuplicate/replace/retain/touch are re-declared only to narrow the return type, so they are inherited from IByteBufHolder and the classes narrow them with covariant overrides (owner decision 2026-11-19; docs/transport-porting.md, Decisions); the comment of the re-declared content() stays in the interface. stream(Http2FrameStream) is re-declared only to narrow the return type, so it is inherited from IHttp2StreamFrame and the classes narrow it (owner decision 2026-11-19). stream() is re-declared with the same type and inherited.
The Java interface takes the I prefix (owner rule). No other CLR difference.

The final class with a private constructor is a static class and the static initializers are static constructors. The codec-http interfaces take the I prefix and their getters are methods (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Messages). The @Deprecated message constructors with a validateHeaders flag are not ported in codec-http (named replacements: the HttpHeadersFactory constructors), so the conversions use the HttpHeadersFactory constructors with headersFactory().withValidation(v)/trailersFactory().withValidation(v), which is what the deprecated Java constructors call. The @Deprecated HttpHeaderNames.KEEP_ALIVE and PROXY_CONNECTION are not ported in codec-http, so the blacklist uses AsciiString constants with the same names. The enum ExtensionHeaderNames (constructor, field, method) is a sealed class with static readonly instances and Values(). HttpHeaders.get returns a string, wrapped in StringCharSequence where Java uses it as a CharSequence; StringUtil.unescapeCsvFields takes and returns strings in the Common port. InternalThreadLocalMap.stringBuilder() is a new StringBuilder. new IllegalStateException(e) keeps the message cause.toString() (ThrowableUtil.ThrowableToString). The == of HttpResponseStatus.SWITCHING_PROTOCOLS is ReferenceEquals. java.net.URI (URI.create, getScheme, getPort, getAuthority) has no BCL counterpart with the same results (System.Uri canonicalizes host case, user info and default ports), so the private CreateUri/UriScheme/UriPort/UriAuthority helpers keep the parts of OpenJDK's URI parser that apply to the two forms this class passes ("" and the scheme://authority text of http2PathlessRequestTarget): an empty authority before "/", "?" or "#" is allowed (getAuthority() null), a reg_name authority (unreserved, %-escapes, visible non-ASCII, "$,;:@&=+") is registry-based when it is not a server, an authority with brackets must parse as [userinfo@][IPv6][:port] (System.Net.IPAddress.TryParse checks the literal), any other character, a malformed escape or a failed server parse throws ArgumentException (URI.create's IllegalArgumentException), getPort() is -1 if undefined and getAuthority() decodes %-escapes as UTF-8 outside brackets. Package-private static methods are internal. Measured with the conversion group's HttpConversionUtilTest cases: absolute-form targets with user info, IPv6 literal, explicit port, "http://?x=1#frag", empty query/fragment, and the malformed "http://[bad host]" give the Java results.

Public class over Http2ConnectionHandler. The four protected constructors are protected internal (the builder creates the handler through Java's package access, as Http2ConnectionHandler's constructors). write(ctx, msg, promise) is the override WriteAsync(ctx, msg, cancellationToken), whose returned Task replaces the promise (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Outbound operations): a message that is not an IHttpMessage/IHttpContent is passed on with ctx.WriteAsync(msg, cancellationToken); otherwise the handler creates the promise (Http2CodecUtil.NewPromise, a TaskCompletionSource) that SimpleChannelPromiseAggregator completes and returns its Task; the token is not used otherwise (Java has none) and the encoder's returned Tasks are discarded as Java ignores the futures. The aggregator's setFailure/newPromise()/doneAllocatingPromises() are the base group's SetFailure/NewPromise/DoneAllocatingPromises. HttpMessage/HttpContent/LastHttpContent/FullHttpMessage are the codec-http I-prefixed interfaces (content() is Content), Throwable is Exception, ReferenceCountUtil.release is the Common ReferenceCountUtil.Release. Measured: a request without a scheme fails the returned Task (testNoSchemeRequestTargetHandled) and stream id -1 fails it with Http2NoMoreStreamIdsException (testInvalidStreamId), as in Java.

Public sealed builder over AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder<HttpToHttp2ConnectionHandler, HttpToHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder>. The @Override methods widen protected builder members to public; a C# override "can't change the accessibility of the virtual method" (override keyword page), so they are public members declared new ("you explicitly hide a member that a base class provides", new modifier page) that call base, as the base group's Http2ConnectionHandlerBuilder does; the abstract build(...) is a protected override. The @Deprecated initialHuffmanDecodeCapacity(int) override has no @deprecated text and names no replacement, so it is ported with the [Obsolete] text of the base member it exposes ("Huffman decoding no longer depends on having a decode capacity."; owner decision 2026-11-16). httpScheme(HttpScheme) is the public HttpScheme(HttpScheme) method (the method and the codec-http type share the name; type lookup is unaffected). SensitivityDetector is IHttp2HeadersEncoder.ISensitivityDetector.

Public class over Http2EventAdapter with the Java members: the overridable methods (FireChannelRead, NewMessage, ProcessHeadersBegin, OnRstStreamRead(IHttp2Stream, IFullHttpMessage)) are virtual and the protected final ones (RemoveMessage, GetMessage, PutMessage) non-virtual; the protected final fields connection/validateHttpHeaders are protected readonly. The protected constructor is protected internal, because InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapterBuilder creates the adapter through Java's package access. The private interface ImmediateSendDetector is the private nested IImmediateSendDetector and the anonymous DEFAULT_SEND_DETECTOR is the private nested DefaultSendDetector. The generic stream property accessors are IHttp2Stream.GetProperty<V>/SetProperty<V>/RemoveProperty<V> with IFullHttpMessage. FullHttpMessage is IFullHttpMessage (content() is the Content property) and FullHttpRequest.replace(ByteBuf) returns IByteBufHolder (narrowing re-declarations are inherited, docs/codec-http-porting.md), so its result is cast to IFullHttpRequest; ctx.alloc() is ctx.Alloc(). The "throws Http2Exception" members throw Http2Exception (no checked exceptions); connectionError/streamError are Http2Exception.ConnectionError/StreamError with the Java format text (Http2CodecUtil.Format). No byte arithmetic.

Public sealed builder over AbstractInboundHttp2ToHttpAdapterBuilder<InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter, InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapterBuilder>. The @Override methods widen protected builder members to public; a C# override "can't change the accessibility of the virtual method" (override keyword page), so they are public members declared new ("you explicitly hide a member that a base class provides", new modifier page) that call base, as the base group's Http2ConnectionHandlerBuilder does; the abstract build(...) is a protected override. MaxContentLength(int), ValidateHttpHeaders(bool), PropagateSettings(bool) and Build() are public new members.

Public class over ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter; channelRead is the ChannelRead override and the package-private static handle(...) is internal static Handle (Http2ServerUpgradeCodec of the multiplex group calls it through Java's package access). FullHttpMessage is IFullHttpMessage, content() is the Content property and trailingHeaders() TrailingHeaders(); HttpScheme.HTTP.name() is the AsciiString Name(). The "throws" clauses have no checked-exception counterpart. No other difference.

java.util.Queue has no BCL interface counterpart: the wrapped queue is the BCL Queue<E>, the counterpart of the ArrayDeque its callers pass (docs/handler-porting.md: ArrayDeque is Queue<T>, peek/poll are TryPeek/TryDequeue and remove() is Dequeue()). The Queue/Collection methods keep their Java names (Add, Offer, Remove(), Poll, Element, Peek, Size, IsEmpty, Contains, ToArray, Remove(object), ContainsAll, AddAll, RemoveAll, RetainAll, Clear) and delegate; iterator() is GetEnumerator() of IEnumerable<E>. Queue<T> cannot remove an arbitrary element, so remove(Object), removeAll and retainAll rebuild the queue in order without the removed elements. Collection<?> is ICollection and Collection<? extends E> is IReadOnlyCollection<E> (docs/codec-http-porting.md). IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException; the package-private class and constructor are internal.

Implements IHttp2Headers over the codec-base IHeaders directly, as in Java: Map.Entry and Iterator are IEntry and IIterator (with the IEnumerator side MoveNext/Current), Iterable<? extends CharSequence>/Iterable<?> are IEnumerable<ICharSequence>/IEnumerable<object>, Headers<? extends CharSequence, ? extends CharSequence, ?> is the generic IHeaders<ICharSequence, ICharSequence, T2> parameter, the boxed getters return bool?/sbyte?/char?/short?/int?/long?/float?/double? (the codec-base byte is sbyte) and GetEnumerator() returns iterator(). AsciiString.hashCode(CharSequence) is AsciiString.HashCode; HashingStrategy is IEqualityComparer. String.valueOf(value) of the contains* methods is the CharSequenceValueConverter text of the value (true/false, invariant numbers, Double.toString through JdkDecimal), and value.toString() of containsObject is ConvertObject (a null value throws NullReferenceException where Java dereferences null). LinkedHashSet is the Common LinkedHashSet, Collections.emptySet() is ImmutableHashSet.Empty, getClass().getSimpleName() is GetType().Name. UnsupportedOperationException is NotSupportedException, NoSuchElementException is InvalidOperationException (IIterator contract), IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException. The inner iterator classes take the ReadOnlyHttp2Headers in their constructors. assert is Debug.Assert.

Public class over DecoratingHttp2ConnectionEncoder. ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource and ChannelFuture is Task; the Task-returning methods take the Async suffix (WriteDataAsync, WriteHeadersAsync, WritePriorityAsync, WriteRstStreamAsync, WriteSettingsAsync, WriteSettingsAckAsync, WritePingAsync, WritePushPromiseAsync, WriteGoAwayAsync, WriteWindowUpdateAsync, WriteFrameAsync) and return the promise's Task (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations; owner rule 2). promise.setFailure(e)/setSuccess() returning the promise are SetException(e)/SetResult() followed by the promise's Task. TreeMap<Integer, PendingStream> is SortedDictionary<int, PendingStream> (docs/codec-http-porting.md: TreeMap is SortedDictionary): pollFirstEntry() is the private CLR helper PollFirstEntry() (take and remove the smallest key), and the removing values() iterator of cancelGoAwayStreams walks a snapshot of the values in key order and removes each cancelled stream by id. ArrayDeque<Frame> is Queue<Frame>. The anonymous Http2ConnectionAdapter of the constructor is the private nested GoAwayAndCloseListener; the inner HeadersFrame/DataFrame classes get the encoder as a constructor argument. GoAwayDetail is internal instead of private, because the internal Http2GoAwayException(GoAwayDetail) constructor takes it (a parameter type cannot be less accessible than its method, CS0051). The nested exceptions Http2ChannelClosedException and Http2GoAwayException keep their Java shape (lastStreamId()/errorCode()/debugData() are methods; byte[].clone() is Array.Clone()); serialVersionUID has no counterpart. close() and the write/remoteSettings methods override the virtual members of DecoratingHttp2FrameWriter/DecoratingHttp2ConnectionEncoder; ReferenceCountUtil.safeRelease is SafeRelease.
The Java interface takes the I prefix (owner rule). The nested interfaces take the I prefix as well. (IStreamState, IWriter).

The Deque<State> is a LinkedList (pollFirst/addFirst/addLast are the first node, AddFirst and AddLast, and remove(Object) is Remove(T), O(n) as in Java); the private Deque.pollFirst() helper returns null for an empty queue. The private method state(Http2Stream) is State_(): it cannot share the name of the nested State class (CS0102, owner rule: trailing underscore). The inner (non-static) classes and the anonymous classes, which are private nested classes, receive the enclosing instance explicitly, because a C# nested class has no enclosing instance. Throwable is Exception; assert is Debug.Assert and its message prints the boolean as true/false (Http2CodecUtil.ToJavaString) and the number with the invariant culture.

IntObjectMap<State>/IntObjectHashMap are Dictionary<int, State> (owner decision 2026-11-19). The IntCollections.emptyMap() of stateOnlyMap (maxStateOnlySize 0) is an empty Dictionary that the code never adds to (every put is guarded by maxStateOnlySize == 0), because IntCollections' empty map returns null from remove(int) where a read-only dictionary throws; the empty children map is the shared EMPTY_CHILDREN sentinel, compared by reference as Java compares IntCollections.emptyMap(), and never added to (initChildrenIfEmpty replaces it first). The Iterator<PrimitiveEntry<State>> through which takeChild removes a child is the Dictionary being enumerated: Iterator.remove() is Dictionary.Remove of the current key, which does not invalidate the enumerator (.NET Core 3.0+). Netty's PriorityQueue, DefaultPriorityQueue, EmptyPriorityQueue and PriorityQueueNode are Common's IPriorityQueue, DefaultPriorityQueue, EmptyPriorityQueue and IPriorityQueueNode (Netty.NET.Common.Internal): peek()/poll()/add()/offer()/size()/removeTyped/containsTyped are TryPeek/TryDequeue/TryEnqueue/Count/Remove/Contains, with private Peek/Poll helpers that return null for an empty queue as Java does. Comparator<State> is IComparer<State> (Serializable and serialVersionUID have no counterpart) and Long.compare is long.CompareTo. The private method state(...) is State_ (CS0102, owner rule). The inner (non-static) classes and the anonymous classes, which are private nested classes, receive the enclosing instance explicitly, because a C# nested class has no enclosing instance. A Java switch on the stream State is an if/else chain on reference equality. The package-private notifyParentChanged is private, because its parameter type ParentChangedEvent is private (CS0051); the test-only isChild/numChildren and INITIAL_CHILDREN_MAP_SIZE are internal (SystemPropertyUtil.GetInt). The flags byte keeps its value: ~STATE_IS_ACTIVE/~STATE_IS_DISTRIBUTING are cast back to byte unchecked, which clears only that bit as Java's byte arithmetic does. Throwable is Exception; assert is Debug.Assert; StringBuilder.setLength is the Length property and numbers in toString() use the invariant culture.

caseMappings.adaptation: Ported 1:1 with xUnit ([Fact]/[Theory]); @Mock fields and initMocks are Moq loose mocks created in the constructor, which runs @BeforeEach, and @AfterEach is Dispose() (xUnit creates a test class instance per test); Mockito when/thenAnswer/doAnswer/verify are Moq Setup(...).Returns/Callback and Verify, a plain verify(mock) is Times.Once() (Mockito's default times(1)), verifyNoMoreInteractions is VerifyNoOtherCalls() and ArgumentCaptor a Callback that stores the argument; assertThrows(T.class) is Assert.ThrowsAny<T> and assertInstanceOf Assert.IsAssignableFrom (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Core test notes). eq(settings) is the value itself, matched with Equals, which Http2Settings overrides with Java's map equality. The private nested interface TestHttp2ConnectionEncoder is the public ITestHttp2ConnectionEncoder, because Moq's Castle DynamicProxy implements it in another assembly and cannot implement a private nested interface.

caseMappings.adaptation: Ported 1:1 with xUnit ([Fact]/[Theory]); @Mock fields and initMocks are Moq loose mocks created in the constructor, which runs @BeforeEach, and @AfterEach is Dispose() (xUnit creates a test class instance per test); Mockito when/thenAnswer/doAnswer/verify are Moq Setup(...).Returns/Callback and Verify, a plain verify(mock) is Times.Once() (Mockito's default times(1)), verifyNoMoreInteractions is VerifyNoOtherCalls() and ArgumentCaptor a Callback that stores the argument; assertThrows(T.class) is Assert.ThrowsAny<T> and assertInstanceOf Assert.IsAssignableFrom (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Core test notes). The generic getProperty/setProperty stubs match any type argument with It.IsAnyType and answer through InvocationFunc over a Dictionary with ReferenceEqualityComparer (IdentityHashMap); the null key that the mocked connection's newKey() returns is stored under a sentinel because Dictionary rejects null keys. AtomicInteger is an int updated with Interlocked. The decoder creates its own promises and passes Task.CompletedTask for ctx.newSucceededFuture(), so the stubs of ctx.newPromise()/newSucceededFuture()/write(...) have no counterpart and the verifications against the stubbed promise/future match any TaskCompletionSource or any successfully completed Task. Strings passed as CharSequence are StringCharSequence values. The private helpers that overload test names (infoHeadersAndTrailersAllowed, dataContentLengthInvalid) take the suffix 0 (xUnit1024). @ParameterizedTest @ValueSource is a [Theory] with InlineData rows; the anonymous verifier is the private nested NotAuthoritativeVerifier; pingReadShouldRespectNoAutoAck calls the [Obsolete] constructor as the source does (CS0612 suppressed locally); Mock.Get reaches the mock of a mocked object.

notApplicableMethods.reason: Exercises a void ChannelPromise: the merged writes must not complete the void promises ("The promises won't be set since there are no listeners"). Java's void promise is never completed because unvoid() returns a new promise; there is no void promise in the port (VoidChannelPromise is JVM-only, "discard the returned Task") and promise.unvoid() is the promise itself, so the same promise completes when the merged frame is written; the merge path is covered by dataFramesShouldMerge.
notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: Merging two DATA payloads written with void promises writes them as one frame and leaves the void promises incomplete.

The static EventLoopGroup of @BeforeAll/@AfterAll only creates the promises of close(Promise): a promise is a TaskCompletionSource (Http2CodecUtil.NewPromise; docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations), so the group and its non-test beforeClass/afterClass have no counterpart; promise.addListener is a continuation of the returned Task on TaskScheduler.Default, CountDownLatch is CountdownEvent and await(5, SECONDS) is Wait(TimeSpan, TestContext.Current.CancellationToken). doAnswer(answer).when(listener).onX(...) is a Moq Setup with a Callback; the Answer classes keep an Answer() method that the callback calls. streamEq is a Moq custom matcher (Match.Create) that matches null or an equal stream, as ArgumentMatchers.isNull()/eq(stream). Endpoint<?> is the non-generic IHttp2Connection.IEndpoint; MAX_VALUE + 1/+ 2 overflow unchecked as in Java; fail(Throwable) is Assert.Fail with the exception's text; the generic getProperty/removeProperty calls name their type argument (string), which Java infers. The answer of ctx.write(msg, promise) is the callback of IChannelHandlerContext.WriteAsync(msg, CancellationToken), the member DefaultHttp2FrameWriter writes through (Http2CodecUtil.Write); it returns the never-completing Task of a TaskCompletionSource that stands for the mocked ChannelFuture. A DefaultChannelPromise is a TaskCompletionSource; ctx.alloc()/channel()/executor() are Alloc() and the Channel/Executor properties. assertEquals(ByteBuf, ByteBuf) is ByteBuf.Equals (IEquatable<ByteBuf>, content comparison). OutOfMemoryError is OutOfMemoryException (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Core test notes). AbstractByteBufAllocator is the Buffer port's AbstractByteBufAllocator (NewHeapBuffer/NewDirectBuffer, IsDirectBufferPooled property). ByteArrayOutputStream is a MemoryStream, Arrays.copyOfRange an array range, String.format("dummy-%d") invariant text, and repeat(...) string.Concat(Enumerable.Repeat(...)), the same text as the format-and-replace trick.
