caseMappings.adaptation: Real NIO sockets as in Java: MultiThreadIoEventLoopGroup(2, NioIoHandler.NewFactory()), ServerBootstrap/Bootstrap with NioServerSocketChannel/NioSocketChannel (src/Netty.NET.Transport/Bootstrapping/ServerBootstrap.cs, src/Netty.NET.Transport/Bootstrapping/Bootstrap.cs); bind(NetUtil.LOCALHOST, 0) is ServerBootstrap.BindAsync(IPAddress, int) with Common's NetUtil.LOCALHOST and the client connects to the bound address. @BeforeEach setup() and @AfterEach shutdown() keep their names and run from IAsyncLifetime.InitializeAsync/DisposeAsync, because sync()/syncUninterruptibly() are awaits of the Transport Tasks (as test/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2.Tests/Http2ConnectionRoundtripTest.cs). ChannelInitializer<SocketChannel> is ChannelInitializer<ISocketChannel> (named nested ServerInitializer/ClientInitializer); the inner ServerHandler takes the test (contentMap) through its constructor. ConcurrentHashMap<Integer, String> is ConcurrentDictionary<int, string> (put the indexer, get TryGetValue yielding null), CountDownLatch CountdownEvent (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations). ctx.writeAndFlush(...).addListener(l) is Http2CodecUtil.AddListener (DefaultPromise listener timing on the event loop, src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2/Http2CodecUtil.cs); writes whose future is unused discard the Task. Java Strings passed as CharSequence are Http2TestUtil.Of; String.getBytes() is Encoding.Default.GetBytes ("String.getBytes() in the tests (default charset) is Encoding.Default", docs/codec-http-porting.md) and CharsetUtil.UTF_8 Encoding.UTF8 (src/Netty.NET.Common/CharsetUtil.cs). As in Java, send() only writes the request; the assertions run in the handlers on the event loop and the graceful shutdown closes the channels at once (Java's NioIoHandler.prepareToDestroy closes every registration when the loop starts shutting down). Measured with a temporary 2 s pause after the write (not part of the port): the client reads PUSH_PROMISE (stream 3, promised 2, the four pseudo-headers), HEADERS and DATA "Meow" on stream 3, then HEADERS and DATA "Meow, I am Pushed via HTTP/2" on stream 2, with no exception. The single declared method is mapped and passes.

caseMappings.adaptation: The package-private class and enum OpenMode are public (xUnit runs public test classes; a theory parameter type must be as accessible as the method, CS0051); @ParameterizedTest @EnumSource(OpenMode.class) is a [Theory] with one InlineData row per constant (3 cases). Real NIO sockets as in Java (MultiThreadIoEventLoopGroup with NioIoHandler, ServerBootstrap/Bootstrap, NioServerSocketChannel/NioSocketChannel); bind(NetUtil.LOCALHOST, 0).sync().channel() is the await of ServerBootstrap.BindAsync(IPAddress, int). Java's Bootstrap.connect() returns a ChannelFuture whose channel() exists before the connect completes, and the test builds the Http2StreamChannelBootstrap on it at once; the Transport's Bootstrap.ConnectAsync() returns Task<IChannel>, which yields the channel only after the connect (src/Netty.NET.Transport/Bootstrapping/Bootstrap.cs). connect() is therefore its two Java steps (Bootstrap.doResolveAndConnect: initAndRegister(), then doConnect's channel.connect(remoteAddress, connectPromise), whose promise connect() returns): Bootstrap.RegisterAsync() gives the registered channel and cf is the Task of channel.ConnectAsync(Config.RemoteAddress), the channel's connect promise, so Http2ConnectionHandler.ConnectAsync (send the preface before completing the connect promise, src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2/Http2ConnectionHandler.cs) is on the path as in Java. ChannelFuture/Future listeners are continuations on Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler over the channel's event loop (DefaultPromise.notifyListeners timing, owner decision 2026-11-24, src/Netty.NET.Common/Concurrent/EventExecutorTaskScheduler.cs); measured: the Listener-mode continuation runs with InEventLoop() true, so the stream is opened on the event loop in the connect notification as in Java. GenericFutureListener<Future<Http2StreamChannel>> is the nested listener's OperationComplete(Task<IHttp2StreamChannel>) (src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2/Http2StreamChannelBootstrap.cs OpenAsync), getNow() the result of a successful Task or null. CompletableFuture<Http2HeadersFrame> is TaskCompletionSource<IHttp2HeadersFrame> with RunContinuationsAsynchronously (so the awaiting test does not resume on the event loop that completes it, as Java's get() waits on the test thread); complete/completeExceptionally are TrySetResult/TrySetException and get(5, SECONDS) WaitAsync(5 s). eventLoop().submit is the Common SubmitAsync extension (src/Netty.NET.Common/Concurrent/EventExecutorExtensions.cs); throw new AssertionError() is UnreachableException (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations); copiedBuffer(s, UTF_8) is Unpooled.CopiedBuffer(s, Encoding.UTF8). The anonymous initializers and adapters are named nested classes (BackendInitializer, ServerStreamInitializer, ClientInitializer, ExceptionForwarder, ResponseHandler). All three rows pass in every run.

caseMappings.adaptation: The 14 JSON test cases are deployed next to the test assembly under io/netty/handler/codec/http2/testdata/ (the test csproj), so TEST_DIR is that path written out (the C# namespace of the test class is not the Java package). ResourcesUtil.getFile is the Common ResourcesUtil.GetFile(Type, string), which resolves against the assembly directory, so the leading "/" of the class-path name is dropped; listFiles() is DirectoryInfo.GetFiles(), getResourceAsStream is File.OpenRead and try-with-resources is using. @ParameterizedTest @MethodSource("files") is a [Theory] with MemberData rows (TheoryData<FileInfo>); the rows are not serializable, so DisableDiscoveryEnumeration lets xUnit enumerate them when the theory runs (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Core test notes). Each row runs HpackTestCase.testCompress/testDecompress.

notApplicableMethods.reason: Http2MultiplexCodec and Http2MultiplexCodecBuilder are @Deprecated with the replacement named ("use Http2FrameCodecBuilder together with Http2MultiplexHandler") and are not ported (owner decision 2026-11-16, deprecated-not-ported). The method only upgrades to a codec built by Http2MultiplexCodecBuilder.forClient(handler).withUpgradeStreamHandler(...); its replacement, Http2FrameCodecBuilder.forClient() with new Http2MultiplexHandler(inbound, upgrade), is the separate method testUpgradeToHttp2FrameCodecWithMultiplexer of the same class, which is ported and passes.
notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: Http2ClientUpgradeCodec(String, Http2ConnectionHandler) with an Http2MultiplexCodec sets the HTTP2-Settings header, adds the codec under the given name on upgradeTo and reserves stream 1, leaving outbound data to release.

caseMappings.adaptation: Ported 1:1 with xUnit; Mockito @Mock fields are Moq Mock<T> created per test (xUnit creates a test class instance per test), @BeforeEach is the constructor, when/doAnswer are Setup(...).Returns/Callback/Throws, verify(..., times/never/atLeastOnce) Verify(..., Times...), clearInvocations Invocations.Clear() and verifyNoMoreInteractions/verifyNoInteractions VerifyNoOtherCalls(); ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource and ChannelFuture Task; assertThrows(T) is Assert.ThrowsAny<T>; assertions with messages use XunitAssertMessages.AssertM. There is no ChannelHandlerContext.newPromise()/voidPromise() in the Transport port: the handler creates its own TaskCompletionSource (Http2CodecUtil.NewPromise), so the stubs of ctx.newPromise()/voidPromise() have no counterpart and eq(promise) for a promise that Java takes from ctx.newPromise() is It.IsAny<TaskCompletionSource>(); the promise the test passes to goAway/resetStream is matched itself. The mocked ChannelFuture (cause() FAKE_EXCEPTION, addListener runs the listener at once) is Task.FromException(FAKE_EXCEPTION), and Task.CompletedTask where the test stubs isDone()/isSuccess() to true. close(ctx, promise) is CloseAsync(ctx, CancellationToken) and its returned Task. The mocked EventExecutor is the private RecordingEventExecutor (an AbstractScheduledEventExecutor that is always in its event loop, runs execute() at once and records the delay of every scheduled task through ValidateScheduled), because ScheduleAsync schedules only on an AbstractScheduledEventExecutor (src/Netty.NET.Common/Concurrent/EventExecutorSchedulingExtensions.cs) and a Moq mock cannot record executor.schedule(...). The ArgumentCaptors are Callback captures; eq(connectionPrefaceBuf()) compares with ByteBuf.Equals; the anonymous Http2ConnectionHandler subclass is the nested PrefaceEventHandler and CountDownLatch is CountdownEvent. The latch waits and the EmbeddedChannel close/connect calls pass TestContext.Current.CancellationToken (xUnit1051).

The anonymous Http2Runnables are the nested ActionRunnable over a lambda, the anonymous ChannelInitializers/handlers are nested classes, CountDownLatch is CountdownEvent (SignalIfPending keeps countDown() at zero a no-op where Signal() throws), AtomicReference/AtomicBoolean/AtomicInteger are locals ordered by the latches, and a ChannelFuture listener is a synchronous Task continuation (Listen). eq(headers) is the expected headers value, which Moq compares with Equals. Future.get() inside assertThrows(ExecutionException) with e.getCause() is Assert.ThrowsAnyAsync of the cause type on the Task (awaiting throws the cause itself), and promise.setFailure(e) in the anonymous ChannelOutboundHandlerAdapter is the failed Task its WriteAsync returns. The repeated "Verify that no errors have been received." checks share the private VerifyNoErrors(). ByteArrayOutputStream is MemoryStream, ThreadLocalRandom.nextBytes Random.Shared.NextBytes and data.array() ByteBufUtil.GetBytes(data).

caseMappings.adaptation: Ported 1:1 with xUnit ([Fact]/[Theory]); @Mock fields and initMocks are Moq loose mocks created in the constructor, which runs @BeforeEach, and @AfterEach is Dispose() (xUnit creates a test class instance per test); Mockito when/thenAnswer/doAnswer/verify are Moq Setup(...).Returns/Callback and Verify, a plain verify(mock) is Times.Once() (Mockito's default times(1)), verifyNoMoreInteractions is VerifyNoOtherCalls() and ArgumentCaptor a Callback that stores the argument; assertThrows(T.class) is Assert.ThrowsAny<T> and assertInstanceOf Assert.IsAssignableFrom (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Core test notes). ChannelPromise is TaskCompletionSource (newPromise() is a new TaskCompletionSource, setSuccess()/setFailure(e) are SetResult()/SetException(e)) and ChannelFuture is Task, whose IsCompleted/IsCompletedSuccessfully are isDone()/isSuccess() and Http2CodecUtil.Cause(task) is cause(). The answers receive the promise argument directly, so handlePromise takes the TaskCompletionSource. The encoder's listeners run on ctx.Executor, the mocked executor whose InEventLoop() is true. ctx.close() is CloseAsync(CancellationToken); channel.unsafe() and the ctx.newPromise() stub have no counterpart. Mockito atLeast(0) holds for any count while Moq's Times.AtLeast needs a positive count, so the flush check runs only for a positive count.

close(p) with a promise created before the close has no counterpart (the ChannelPromise overloads fold into CloseAsync(), docs/transport-porting.md, Decisions), so the listener is added to the Task of CloseAsync() (the child channel's own close promise), which is already complete when CloseAsync() returns (measured), so the listener runs at once; it records isOpen()/isActive() of the child channel (future.channel()). The listener is added to CloseFuture before the close, as in Java, and runs on the event loop when AbstractChannel completes CloseFuture there; the test asserts that the channel was neither open nor active when closeFuture completed.

ChannelFuture is Task and ChannelPromise TaskCompletionSource; the ChannelPromise overloads fold into the Task-returning members (docs/transport-porting.md, Decisions) and a void promise is a discarded Task (docs/transport-porting.md, Not-ported Transport sources: VoidChannelPromise). syncUninterruptibly() is an await (the tests that wait are async), awaitUninterruptibly() an await with ConfigureAwaitOptions.SuppressThrowing | ContinueOnCapturedContext (docs/handler-porting.md, Test notes: ChunkedWriteHandlerTest; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.configureawaitoptions?view=net-10.0), isDone() IsCompleted, isSuccess() IsCompletedSuccessfully and cause() Http2CodecUtil.Cause. The EmbeddedChannel completes every operation on the test thread, so every awaited Task is already complete, as Java's syncUninterruptibly() on an EmbeddedEventLoop requires. The Channel getters are IChannel properties (src/Netty.NET.Transport/Channels/IChannel.cs); Http2StreamChannel is IHttp2StreamChannel and Http2Stream.State the sealed class IHttp2Stream.State. Listeners added by the test (closeFuture()/close(promise)/write future addListener) are continuations on Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler over the channel's event loop, the DefaultPromise.notifyListeners() timing (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Listener timing; src/Netty.NET.Common/Concurrent/EventExecutorTaskScheduler.cs), with ExecuteSynchronously (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.taskcontinuationoptions?view=net-10.0): the child channel's write and close Tasks are its own promises without asynchronous continuations, so a listener runs where the promise completes, before the test asserts, as in Java. ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE inside a child handler is Http2CodecUtil.AddListener closing ctx.Channel. Java's ClosedChannelException is the Transport's (src/Netty.NET.Transport/Channels/ClosedChannelException.cs), RuntimeException Exception and assertThrows Assert.ThrowsAny/ThrowsAnyAsync (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Core test notes); the JUnit message overloads use XunitAssertMessages.AssertM, HttpHeaders equality calls Equals directly, and Java Strings passed as CharSequence are Http2TestUtil.Of. new Thread(runnable, "setAutoRead-hammer") is a Thread with that Name, setDaemon(true) IsBackground = true (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.thread.isbackground?view=net-10.0), join(5000) Join(5000) and interrupt() Interrupt(). LockSupport.parkNanos(1000) ("for up to the specified waiting time", https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/util/concurrent/locks/LockSupport.html) is Thread.Yield(): the BCL has no timed sleep below a whole millisecond (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.thread.sleep?view=net-10.0), and Thread.Sleep(1) toggled setAutoRead only 5 times per transfer in 3 measured runs (about 70 ms each; HotSpot on Windows also coarsens such a park to 1 ms, Parker::park in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openjdk/jdk17u/master/src/hotspot/os/windows/os_windows.cpp), which defeats the source's "hammering setAutoRead() as fast as possible"; Thread.Yield() gives up the time slice without a timed wait (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.thread.yield?view=net-10.0): 164 921 to 193 103 toggles per transfer in 3 measured runs, all passing (Thread.SpinWait(20): 47 758 to 67 075). caseMappings.adaptation: group.execute(Runnable) is Execute(Action) on the single event loop, which blocks in closeLatch.Wait() and then waits for the client channel's close Task inside the loop (GetAwaiter().GetResult(): the local channel completes the close it runs on its own loop, as Java's sync finds the future done). clientChannel.eventLoop().newPromise() is a new TaskCompletionSource<IHttp2StreamChannel>; open(promise) queues Open0 behind the blocked task, so promise.isDone() (Task.IsCompleted) is false. promise.get(3, SECONDS) throwing ExecutionException with a ClosedChannelException cause is Assert.ThrowsAnyAsync<ClosedChannelException> on promise.Task.WaitAsync(3 s, token): awaiting the Task throws the cause itself (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Core test notes). group.shutdownGracefully(0, 3 s) is not awaited, as in the source.

The @Deprecated open0(ChannelHandlerContext, Promise), whose @deprecated text names open() and open(Promise), is not ported as a public member: its body is the private Open0 that OpenAsync runs (src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2/Http2StreamChannelBootstrap.cs). The test checks that body's behaviour (newOutboundStream throws, the promise fails), so it runs through the named replacement OpenAsync(promise): the mocked IChannel's Pipeline returns the mocked context for Context(typeof(Http2MultiplexHandler)), which is how open(Promise) finds the context the source passes directly, and the mocked executor's InEventLoop() is true, so Open0 runs at once as the direct call does. new DefaultPromise<>(mock(EventExecutor.class)) is a TaskCompletionSource<IHttp2StreamChannel>, promise.cause() Http2CodecUtil.Cause(task), and IllegalStateException InvalidOperationException, which Http2ChannelDuplexHandler.NewStream throws before the handler was added (src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2/Http2ChannelDuplexHandler.cs); assertInstanceOf is Assert.IsAssignableFrom (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Core test notes).

review.scope: JUnit 5 tests become xUnit v3 tests with the same names (first letter upper case). The Local transport is the Transport port (MultiThreadIoEventLoopGroup(1, LocalIoHandler.NewFactory()), LocalServerChannel, LocalChannel; docs/transport-porting.md, Tests); new LocalAddress(getClass().getName()) is LocalAddress(GetType().FullName) (docs/common-clr-design.md, Source class names in text); sync()/syncUninterruptibly() is awaiting the Task; Promise<Http2StreamChannel> is TaskCompletionSource<IHttp2StreamChannel> and open(promise) OpenAsync(promise) (src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2/Http2StreamChannelBootstrap.cs); the anonymous ChannelInitializer bodies are ActionChannelInitializer delegates (docs/transport-porting.md); CountDownLatch is CountdownEvent (docs/handler-porting.md, SSL tests); Mockito mock/when(...).thenReturn is Moq Mock<T>/Setup(...).Returns (docs/codec-http-porting.md, Shared CLR adaptations); InterruptedException is ThreadInterruptedException (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.thread.interrupt?view=net-10.0); logger.error(e) is IInternalLogger.Error(Exception); safeClose(Channel) returns a Task because close().syncUninterruptibly() is awaiting the close Task. Both declared methods are mapped and pass (23 runs of the two classes, 6 runs of the whole scratch test project). No byte value is involved.

caseMappings.adaptation: testSerialization is ported with the Transport's replacement of Java object serialization: ObjectOutputStream/ObjectInputStream have no CLR counterpart, and the Transport channel-ID tests round-trip the concrete ID through System.Text.Json (test/Netty.NET.Transport.Tests/DefaultChannelIdTest.cs, test/Netty.NET.Transport.Tests/EmbeddedChannelIdTest.cs; docs/transport-porting-manifest.json, DefaultChannelId decision 2026-11-16: "The concrete ID JSON converters carry the long text; Java binary serialization and arbitrary interface polymorphism are not provided"). Http2StreamChannelId has no JSON converter of its own (src/Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Http2/Http2StreamChannelId.cs: serialVersionUID has no counterpart), so the test registers the nested Http2StreamChannelIdConverter in JsonSerializerOptions.Converters, which ranks above a [JsonConverter] on the type ("Converter registration precedence", https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/converters-how-to). It writes Java's two serialized fields, parentId (through DefaultChannelId's own JSON contract, the long text; src/Netty.NET.Transport/Channels/DefaultChannelId.cs) and id, and reads them into a new instance through the internal constructor (the tests see internals). The JSON still goes through ByteBufOutputStream/ByteBufInputStream(buf, true) over Unpooled.Buffer() as in the source, close() is Dispose() (docs/buffer-porting.md, Input and Output stream adapters), and System.IO.Stream is qualified because Stream binds to the Netty.NET.Handler.Stream namespace. ChannelId is IChannelId, DefaultChannelId.newInstance() is NewInstance(), compareTo/asLongText/asShortText are CompareTo/AsLongText/AsShortText and hashCode() is GetHashCode(). The five assertions are unchanged; the declared method passes.

notPorted.sourceContract: Jazzer @FuzzTest currentConversionMatchesOldUriBasedConversion(FuzzedDataProvider) (maxDuration 30s, class enabled only with JAZZER_FUZZ=1): for fuzzed request targets of at most 128 characters, HttpConversionUtil.toHttp2Headers(msg, false) must give the same scheme, authority and method as the old java.net.URI-based conversion (oldToHttp2Headers and its helpers) and the same path except for five known compatibility forms. @FuzzTest is not a JUnit @Test, so the test inventory declares no method for this class.
notPorted.reason: Owner decision 2026-11-25 (codec-http2 brief, decision 5): jazzer, a test-only third-party library, has no BCL counterpart, so the fuzz test is library-not-ported. "Jazzer is a coverage-guided, in-process fuzzer for the JVM platform"; its JUnit integration runs @FuzzTest methods in regression mode by default and fuzzes only after "setting the environment variable JAZZER_FUZZ=1" (Jazzer README). The FuzzedDataProvider input and the coverage-guided engine are JVM-only; the .NET 10 BCL has no fuzzing engine and no third-party test library is added.

replacement.clr: None: the fuzz test is left out. The behaviour it fuzzes is covered by the ported HttpConversionUtilTest, whose absolute-form, origin-form, empty, query/fragment and malformed request-target cases run against the same HttpConversionUtil.ToHttp2Headers.
noClrCounterpart: A coverage-guided fuzzing engine and FuzzedDataProvider in the .NET 10 BCL.

comments.reason: Original comments of a unit that is not ported because it needs Jazzer.

notPorted.sourceContract: Runs ChannelHandlerMetadataUtil.generateMetadata(io.netty.handler.codec.http2), which scans the package(s) for ChannelHandler subtypes and compares them with the committed GraalVM reflect-config.json.
notPorted.reason: Owner decision 2026-11-16 (as for the Transport ChannelHandlerMetadataUtil): GraalVM reflection JSON, Java package scanning and JVM type names are not consumed by the CLR; NativeAOT keeps handler metadata through DynamicallyAccessedMembers.

replacement.clr: IChannelHandler/ChannelHandlerAdapter DynamicallyAccessedMembers annotations; the Transport NativeAOT scenarios exercise handler dispatch under trimming.
noClrCounterpart: Generating or comparing a reflect-config.json metadata file.
